description: Use it when the user wants screenshots of a site, App Store or Google Play screenshots, Product Hunt gallery images, or a web app manifest's screenshots. Opens a website in a headless browser, picks the pages worth showing (home, pricing, features and the like), hides cookie banners, chat bubbles and other floating boxes, and saves desktop, phone and whole-page screenshots in one folder. sheet.png, every page on one picture, is the picture to show first; SCREENSHOTS.md lists each page with why it was picked, its files and its headings. url and page are pages of one public site: a #route, like /app/#/plants, opens that view of a web app, nothing behind a login is reached, and above one page it starts at the site's root. clean hides everything fixed on the screen but a top bar and a side bar, so an app's own tab bar too. iphone is 1320x2868, the App Store's 6.9 inch size; mobile is 1080x1920, for Google Play phones. For the Google Play feature graphic and Chrome Web Store tiles, use make_launch_stills instead. For a view behind a click, use record_demo_video with steps. The screenshots playbook (makersmcp_playbook) has the whole job. (easyscreenshotkit 0.1.3, on this machine.)

clean.description: Set to false to take the pages as they come; hide still hides what it names. Otherwise cookie banners, chat bubbles and everything else fixed on the screen are hidden, except a bar along its top and a tall bar down a side, so an app's own bottom tab bar is hidden too.

hide.description: CSS selectors of more elements to hide, like .promo-bar, when something still covers a page.

lang.description: The site's version in this language, when it has one: a language code like de, tr or pt-BR.

out_dir.description: Folder to save into, absolute or relative to /tmp/churn-hnvpfmca. Default: easyscreenshotkit-<host>, where <host> is the site's host without www or the port. A run replaces what an earlier run of this tool left there once it has ended well, and one that fails or is canceled leaves it as it was: give each version its own out_dir. The folder must be empty or hold an earlier run of this tool: any other folder stops it.

page.description: Pages of the same site to take too, like /pricing, or views of a web app by their #route, like /app/#/plants; #/plants alone is that view of url. Each counts toward pages and is taken even past it, and with pages 1 only url and these are taken. Another fragment, like #pricing, is left out.

pages.description: How many pages, the home page included (default 5). Above 1 the site's root comes first, then url when it is a deeper page, then each page, then pages from the site's menu. With 1, only url and each page are taken, as given; a page that is not of the site stops the run.

pwa.description: Also save screenshots for a web app manifest in pwa/: each page's first screen at 1920x1080 and on a phone at 1080x1920, at most 8 in all, checked against Chrome's rules for its richer install dialog, with the manifest entries in pwa/manifest-screenshots.json.

reduced_motion.description: Ask the site for its reduced-motion version.

sizes.description: Any of desktop (3200x1800), mobile (1080x1920, a Google Play phone screenshot), iphone (1320x2868, the App Store's 6.9 inch size), full (the whole page at 1x), mobile-full (the whole phone page at 2x), or WxH from 240 to 3840 a side, like 1270x760 for a Product Hunt gallery image. Each takes an optional @scale from 0.5 to 4, and each size goes in once (default desktop, mobile and full).

theme.description: The site's light or dark look, or both, which adds a -dark twin of every picture (default light). A site without a dark theme looks the same in both.

timeout_seconds.description: Give up after this many seconds (default 300). A run takes two or three minutes, up to five on very long pages, and a slow site can take 600.

url.description: The website, like https://linear.app, or a page of it. A #route in it, like https://acme.app/app/#/plants, opens that view of the app; another fragment, like #pricing, is left out.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the result, counted from the start of the call, before returning a job_id to wait on. Some clients end a call after 60 or 240 seconds; 45 is safe in all of them.

name: take_screenshots

continued.description: True when this call continued the job an identical call started, instead of starting another.

docs.description: The notes the text shows, and where each one is.

expires_at.description: When the download links stop working.

url.description: Where to download the file, when the job ran on a server.

folder.description: Where the kit saved its files.

last_line.description: What the kit was doing last.

next.description: What to do next, as the Next line says.

passed.description: For checks: whether the check passed.

title: Screenshots of a website
